gappers.catalyst: No company-specific news; drone complex bouncing with the broad AI/high-beta tape after a 47% one-month drawdown, against a Nov 24 WSJ report that the Pentagon is in talks with GM on drone production.
gappers.catalyst_detail: No UMAC-specific news on the tape. The move is the drone complex re-rating with the broad high-beta bounce: Nasdaq 100 futures +2.3-2.9%, NVDA +4%, AMD +5-7% premarket. UMAC had fallen ~47% in a month into Nov 24. The live sector overhang is a Nov 24 WSJ report that the Pentagon is in talks with General Motors about drone production, read as a competitive threat to small suppliers. Oppenheimer initiated Outperform/$30 on Nov 19 and the stock fell the next day; a CRO and the president both reported small pre-arranged insider sales (Nov 26 and earlier), and a Nov 13 filing registered shares from two prior deals for resale.
gappers.why: Pure sector beta, not company news. UMAC is a high-short-interest, low-float drone supplier that moves as a leveraged proxy on risk appetite; when the AI/high-beta complex bounces, it bounces hardest. There is no new information about UMAC's business in today's move.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day headline-free bounce, not a repair. The gap is +0.54 ATR against a 12.5% ATR - well inside one normal session's range, so it is noise, not a breakout. Prior-session volume (2.58M) is below the 20-day average (3.35M), so there is no volume confirmation. Sector read-through is total: ONDS (+6.19%) and RCAT (+6.82%, screened out on the $3 price floor) are moving in lockstep, which confirms beta rather than a UMAC thesis. The GM/Pentagon competitive overhang is unresolved and structurally bearish for a component supplier.
gappers.horizon_reason: Headline-free sector bounce with an unresolved competitive overhang and no durable thesis; price is 48.3% below its 200-SMA.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing - the account holds zero positions and has used 0 of 3 weekly trades, so there is no weaker holding to rotate out of. The real cost is one of three weekly trade slots on the lowest-quality setup on this list. It cannot clear 2:1 R:R at a sane stop: a 1-ATR stop is 12.5% wide, so the minimum target is +25% ($12.16), which is above the 50-SMA ($17.07 is further still) and implausible inside a week. The mandatory 10% trailing GTC stop sits at only 0.8 ATR - closer than one normal day's range - so it would be stopped out by noise before the thesis resolved. Fails the 200-SMA long-bias filter outright. NO-GO.

gappers.catalyst: No company-specific news today; rebounding with the AI-power/data-center complex after Morgan Stanley reiterated a $335 target on Nov 25 calling shares an attractive entry.
gappers.catalyst_detail: No BE-specific news today. Bloom is rebounding with the AI-power/data-center complex. The most recent company-relevant item is Morgan Stanley reiterating a $335 target on Nov 25 and calling the shares an attractive entry point, on a day the stock still fell ~11%. BMO upgraded to Outperform on Nov 19 while cutting its target to $230. Fundamentals are genuinely strong: Q3 revenue $1.235B, +138.1% year over year, 2026 guidance raised to $4.4-4.6B, and NTT DATA plus Google fuel-cell deals announced Nov 5 totaling 1,602MW - yet the stock fell ~16% the following day. Q3 operating cash flow was negative $27.1M as working capital absorbed cash.
gappers.why: Sector beta on an AI-infrastructure bounce, layered on a stock whose fundamentals have been improving while its multiple compresses. The mechanism today is risk appetite returning to AI-power names, not new Bloom information - the Nov 20 15.3% single-day drop came with no announcement, earnings or filing, and all 17 peers above $2B fell with it.
gappers.impact: The highest-quality name on this list on fundamentals, and still not a tradeable setup today. The gap is +0.50 ATR on a 13.0% ATR - inside normal range. Prior-session volume (18.7M) is roughly in line with the 18.0M 20-day average, so no confirmation. Sector read-through is broad: FuelCell -7% and Plug -6% on Nov 25 moved as a group. The stock has round-tripped 170.98 -> 142.39 -> 168.15 -> 152.89 in six sessions; that is a 10-15% daily-range regime in which a 7% gap carries no signal. Price is 27.0% below the 200-SMA - the shallowest breach here, but still a fail.
gappers.horizon_reason: The catalyst set is structural - 138% revenue growth, raised guidance, 1,602MW of signed data-center capacity, two analysts defending $230-335 - and AI/data-center power aligns with the Technology leg of the sector-rotation table; worth a multi-day swing IF it reclaims the 200-SMA and clears Confluence on a later /trade check.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (zero positions, 0/3 weekly trades used). Among today's own list this is the one name whose thesis would survive the gap fading, so spending a weekly slot here costs least - but it is still premature. R:R is the binding problem: a 1-ATR stop is 13.0% ($142.27, below the Nov 20 low of $140.69), requiring a +26% target near $206 for 2:1. That is reachable against the $230-335 analyst range, so the math works on paper - but the mandatory 10% trailing GTC stop is only 0.77 ATR away, so noise stops it out first. This is the unresolved 10%-stop vs 2:1-R:R conflict, made worse by a 13% ATR. WATCH, do not enter; revisit if it reclaims $224 (200-SMA) on above-average volume.

gappers.catalyst: No fresh news; low-priced high-beta bounce after a Nov 9 Q3 EPS miss (2c vs 3c), three target cuts on Nov 10, and a Nov 26 Pomerantz class-action investor alert.
gappers.catalyst_detail: No fresh BW news. The move is a low-priced high-beta bounce on a stock with deteriorating company-specific facts: Q3 2026 reported Nov 9 missed at 2c EPS versus 3c consensus; on Nov 10 Northland cut its target to $15 from $23, Craig-Hallum to $10 from $20, and Needham to $15 from $20. Pomerantz Law Firm issued another investor alert on a securities class action as recently as Nov 26. The balance sheet shows $166.4M of secured debt and bonds against $128.9M of cash and restricted cash; the company did fully redeem its 6.5% bonds due December 2026 and has a $50M repurchase authorization.
gappers.why: Beta plus a low nominal share price. At $4 a 26-cent move is 6.95%, so BW gaps on order flow that would be rounding error in a higher-priced name. No new information - the earnings miss, the target cuts and the active class action all predate today and all cut the other way.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day spike likely to mean-revert, and the weakest fundamental story on the list. The gap is +0.45 ATR on a 14.4% ATR - noise. Prior-session volume (4.37M) is below the 5.74M 20-day average: no confirmation. Price is 63.6% below the 200-SMA, the second-worst breach here, and 81.8% off its 52-week high. An active securities class action with a Dec 15 lead-plaintiff window is an unquantified headline risk that can reprice the stock independently of the tape.
gappers.horizon_reason: Headline-free bounce in a name with an earnings miss, three target cuts and a live class action; nothing structural repaired and price is 63.6% below its 200-SMA.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing on the book, but it would be the worst use of a weekly trade slot on this list - it is strictly dominated by BE, which has the same sector tailwind with growing revenue instead of an earnings miss and a lawsuit. Cannot clear 2:1 R:R: a 1-ATR stop is 14.4% ($3.42), needing a +29% target of $5.16 - above the 50-SMA of $4.85 and against three analysts who just cut to $10-15 on a broken story. The 10% trailing stop sits 0.70 ATR away and would be hit by ordinary chop. Fails the 200-SMA filter. NO-GO.

gappers.catalyst: No company-specific news; neocloud names rallying 8-9.5% premarket with the AI rebound after NBIS closed near a 52-week low on Nov 25.
gappers.catalyst_detail: No NBIS-specific news today; neocloud names are the highest-beta expression of the AI bounce, with CoreWeave and Nebius both quoted up 8-9.5% premarket in reporting. Nebius closed near its 52-week low on Nov 25 after falling ~11% as QQQ fell nearly 4% and HPE's weak margin outlook raised doubts about AI-infrastructure profitability. The structural problem is from Q3 on Nov 12: shares fell sharply on a LOWERED 2026 revenue outlook and disclosed data-center delays, and the company guided to $40-45B of 2027 capex against only $12-13B of 2027 revenue, to be funded largely by customer prepayments and asset-backed loans. A death cross (50-SMA below 200-SMA) formed in November. Citigroup kept Buy but cut its target from $324 to $265.
gappers.why: Leveraged sector beta. NBIS is a capex-heavy, externally-funded AI buildout story, so it trades as a high-duration proxy on both AI sentiment and funding costs - which is why it fell hardest on HPE's margin warning and bounces hardest when risk returns. Today's move contains no new Nebius information.
gappers.impact: The least meaningful gap on the entire list in volatility terms: +6.46% is only +0.31 ATR against a 19.5% ATR - under a third of one normal session's range. Prior-session volume (40.8M) is above the 33.5M 20-day average, the one name here with a volume tick-up, but on a bounce day that reflects sector flow rather than accumulation. The stock reversed most of a 20% Monday gain within two sessions, which is the pattern to expect again. Price is 49.7% below the 200-SMA with a confirmed death cross. The $40-45B capex against $12-13B revenue, funded by prepayments and asset-backed loans, is a genuine solvency-sensitive structure if AI credit tightens into the Dec 8-9 FOMC.
gappers.horizon_reason: Despite a structural-looking capex story, the Q3 guidance cut and data-center delays moved the thesis the wrong way; this is a technical bounce from a 52-week low inside a death cross, not a regime change.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing displaced on the book. Against today's list it would displace BE, which has the same AI-power tailwind with raised rather than lowered guidance - a strictly better version of the same bet. R:R is structurally unreachable: a 1-ATR stop is 19.5% wide ($72.84, below the $73.52 52-week low), demanding a +39% target near $126 for 2:1, which is above the 50-SMA of $174 only in the sense that it is nowhere near it, and implausible in days. The 10% trailing GTC stop is just 0.51 ATR - half a normal day - so it is the single most certain noise stop-out on this list. Fails the 200-SMA filter. NO-GO.

gappers.catalyst: No company-specific news; quantum complex bouncing with high-beta risk-on after a 42% one-month drawdown and a Nov 10 Q3 miss (-$0.13 vs -$0.10).
gappers.catalyst_detail: No QBTS-specific news. The quantum complex is bouncing with high-beta risk-on after a 42% one-month drawdown; MarketBeat noted a similar +12.1% move on Nov 23 during the last bounce, so this is a repeating pattern. Q3 on Nov 10 missed: revenue ~$4.5M and a net loss of $0.13 per share against a $0.10 expected loss, with gross margin falling to 52.9% from 71.4% as lower-margin professional services took more of the mix. The $8.08 close on Nov 17 was its lowest of the year. Peers confirm it is sector-wide: IonQ -28% and Rigetti -34% over the same stretch. Balance sheet is the genuine strength - $503M of cash and short-term investments against $56.9M of total debt. A securities class action is being advertised with a Dec 15, 2026 lead-plaintiff deadline.
gappers.why: Sector beta on a pre-revenue-scale story. With only ~$4.5M of quarterly revenue, QBTS has effectively no earnings anchor, so its price is almost entirely a function of discount rates and risk appetite - it rises mechanically when high-beta risk returns and falls hardest when rate-hike odds rise. Nothing about D-Wave changed today.
gappers.impact: One-day spike, likely to mean-revert - and it has already done exactly this once this month. The gap is +0.45 ATR on a 13.4% ATR: noise. Prior-session volume (20.4M) is above the 17.2M 20-day average, but the Nov 23 precedent shows a +12% bounce in this name fading within two sessions. Price is 58.6% below the 200-SMA and 80.2% off its 52-week high. Real near-term catalysts do exist - delivery of a $20M Florida Atlantic University system is due in fiscal Q4 with substantial revenue booked on delivery, and there is a DoC agreement for up to $100M of CHIPS funding tied to milestones - but neither is today's news and next earnings is not until February 2027.
gappers.horizon_reason: Headline-free sector bounce with a Q3 miss, margin compression and an 80% drawdown; the FAU delivery and CHIPS milestones are real but unscheduled and not today's driver.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing displaced on the book. Within today's list it ranks below BE on every dimension except cash-to-debt. Cannot clear 2:1 R:R: a 1-ATR stop is 13.4% ($6.45), requiring a +27% target of $9.45 - below the 50-SMA of $12.23, so the target is technically reachable, but it sits directly under heavy overhead supply from the entire Nov decline. The 10% trailing GTC stop is 0.75 ATR away and gets hit by ordinary chop. Fails the 200-SMA filter. A rate-sensitive, no-earnings-anchor name is also the worst thing to hold into a Dec 8-9 FOMC with 50bp tail risk. NO-GO.
